title: The earth is spread out for you. Watch the footsteps.
subtitle: Wide permission, and an enemy who walks in steps

row.title: Satan's footsteps
sub: one small step at a time

then: After stating that He alone created everything, Allah reminds people He is also their Provider: {reward}eat from what is lawful and good on the earth.{/reward} Ibn Kathir explains Satan's footsteps as {trap}his ways and methods{/trap}, like the Jahiliyyah custom of forbidding certain camels to honor idols. Qatadah said every act of disobedience is one of his steps.
now: Nobody wakes up and decides to wreck their life. It starts with one late night, one "just this once," one oath sworn in anger. {trap}Footsteps, not leaps.{/trap} Meanwhile {reward}so much good is open to you{/reward} that you barely notice it.
old: Small slips do not really lead anywhere.
new: Satan works in small steps, and Allah has opened far more good than I need.
try: Notice one small step you keep taking toward a habit you dislike. Skip it once today.

title: His worst order: speak about Allah without knowing.
subtitle: Three things Satan commands
then: Ibn Kathir reads the verse as climbing: Satan commands {trap}evil acts, then worse, then what is worse still{/trap}, which is {trap}saying about Allah what you do not know.{/trap} He notes this includes every innovator and disbeliever.
now: Someone in the family group chat forwards a post: "Allah will definitely punish anyone who..." No source, just certainty. You almost forward it too. {idea}Pausing before you speak for Allah is a form of respect.{/idea}
old: Sharing what I think about religion is just my opinion.
new: Speaking about Allah without knowledge is serious. "I do not know" is safer.
try: Before forwarding the next religious message, check its source or let it go.

title: We do what our fathers did. Even if they were wrong?
subtitle: Habit inherited is not the same as guidance
then: When called to what Allah revealed, people answered: {trap}rather, we will follow what we found our fathers doing.{/trap} Ibn 'Abbas said it came about a group who refused the Prophet's ﷺ call this way. The verse asks: {idea}even if their fathers had no understanding or guidance?{/idea}
now: "This is how it has always been done in our family." At weddings, in how daughters are treated, in grudges between relatives. Some of it is beautiful and some of it is not. {idea}The question is not who did it first, but whether Allah approves of it.{/idea}
old: If my family has always done it, it must be fine.
new: I honor my family by keeping what is right and leaving what is not.
try: Name one family custom you follow without thinking. Ask honestly if it pleases Allah.

title: Hearing the call but catching only noise.
subtitle: When words reach the ears but not the heart
then: Ibn Kathir explains the parable: like animals that hear the shepherd but {trap}only catch the sounds, not the meaning.{/trap} Deaf, because they do not hear the truth. Mute, because they do not say it. {trap}Blind, because they do not see its path.{/trap}
now: The Friday talk plays while you check your phone. The Quran recitation runs in the car as background. Your mother's advice comes in one ear. {idea}Sound arrives every day. Meaning only arrives when you lean in.{/idea}
old: I hear plenty of reminders, so I am fine.
new: Hearing the call is not the same as taking it in.
try: Listen to one short reminder today with the phone face down, start to finish.

title: Eat the good things, then say thank you.
subtitle: Food, gratitude, and a dua that rises

row.title: be grateful
sub: if He is whom you worship

then: Allah commands the believers to eat from the good things He provided and {idea}thank Him for it.{/idea} Ibn Kathir cites the hadith of the dusty traveller raising his hands, {trap}'O Lord, O Lord', while his food was unlawful{/trap}, and says pure food is a cause for {reward}supplications being accepted.{/reward}
now: Lunch at your desk, eaten while answering emails. Dinner in front of a screen. You cannot remember tasting it. {idea}The verse pairs eating with thanking, as if the meal is not finished until you say it.{/idea} And where your money comes from reaches your dua.
old: Food is just fuel. What matters is what I do after.
new: What I eat, and how I earned it, and whether I thank Him, are part of my worship.
try: At your next meal, stop for ten seconds and thank Allah for one thing on the plate.

title: Only a few things forbidden, and mercy even in need.
subtitle: A short list, and a door for the desperate
then: After commanding the believers to eat from the good, Allah names {idea}only a short list{/idea} of what He forbade. Ibn Kathir cites the hadith: {reward}what Allah has not mentioned is part of what He has pardoned.{/reward} Even the list ends with mercy for someone driven by real need.
now: A friend says your faith is "just a list of things you cannot do." Look again at the verse. {reward}The field is wide; the fence is short.{/reward} And the One who drew it ends by calling Himself Forgiving and Merciful.
old: Being religious means living mostly with restrictions.
new: Allah opened most things and limited a few, and even then He is merciful.
try: List five good things you enjoyed today that Allah made freely lawful. Thank Him for them.

title: Truth sold for a small price is a terrible trade.
subtitle: Hiding what is right to keep a position
then: Ibn Kathir says those who hid what their Book said did so {trap}to keep the authority, gifts, and honor{/trap} they enjoyed. Yet Allah made the truth known anyway, and the people they feared losing followed it. {trap}Allah will not speak to them nor purify them.{/trap}
now: You keep quiet about a problem at work because speaking up might cost your promotion. You leave out a detail so a sale goes through. {trap}A small price for something priceless.{/trap} {idea}The truth usually comes out anyway. Only the trade remains.{/idea}
old: Bending the truth a little to protect my position is just being smart.
new: Anything I gain by hiding the truth is a small price for a huge loss.
try: Think of one place you stay quiet for gain. Decide what you would say if you were brave.

title: They bought error and paid with guidance.
subtitle: Looking at what you are really paying
then: The verse describes the same people as traders who {trap}purchased error at the price of guidance{/trap} and punishment at the price of forgiveness. It ends with a cry of astonishment at how they could bear what they chose. Ibn Kathir adds: {idea}we seek refuge with Allah from this evil end.{/idea}
now: Every choice has a price tag you do not see at checkout. The extra hour online paid for with fajr. The angry text paid for with a friendship. {idea}Before you buy, read what you are paying with.{/idea}
old: I am not giving anything up, just getting what I want.
new: Every wrong choice is paid for with something good I could have had.
try: Before one tempting choice today, ask: what am I paying for this?

title: The Book came with truth; disputing it pushes people far apart.
subtitle: Why the Book itself is the anchor
then: Ibn Kathir explains the punishment is because Allah's Books {idea}bring truth and expose falsehood{/idea}, and they {idea}ordered people to announce the truth and spread the knowledge.{/idea} Instead, some defied that knowledge, and {trap}those who disputed over the Book ended far away in opposition.{/trap}
now: A study circle turns into a shouting match about who is right. Two cousins stop speaking over an online debate. {trap}The Book becomes a weapon instead of a light.{/trap} {idea}It was sent to guide you, not to win with.{/idea}
old: Arguing hard about religion shows I care.
new: The Book is truth to follow and share, not a stage for disputes that divide.
try: Next time a religious argument heats up, ask what the verse is asking you to do, then stop.

title: Righteousness is not a direction. It is a life.
subtitle: What birr actually looks like

row.title: belief
sub: Allah, Last Day, angels, Book, prophets

then: After all the debate over the Qiblah, Ibn Kathir says this verse makes clear the aim was {idea}obedience to Allah{/idea}, not a direction for its own sake. Then it fills in what righteousness looks like, starting with giving wealth while loving it. The Prophet ﷺ said the best charity is {reward}given while healthy and fearing poverty.{/reward}
now: You arrive early for prayer, perfect row. Then in the car you ignore your brother's call for help with rent, and break a promise to your daughter. {idea}The verse widens the picture: belief, giving, prayer, keeping your word, and steadiness when it hurts.{/idea}
old: If I get the rituals right, I am righteous.
new: Righteousness is faith that shows in my wallet, my promises, and my patience.
try: Give something today you would rather keep, to a relative if you can.
